rv.q: August Wilson’s verbose Pulitzer-winner hits hard in Daniel Bailey’s heavyweight revival
Daniel Bailey’s dynamic production pulses with the jazz played by Lyons, weaving music around the taut scenes.
Conviction and powerful authority are the hallmarks of every performance in this fizzing and compelling masterwork.
Wilson has written a fascinating psychological portrait within a play which is both epic and soapy, the latter in the best possible way.
Headlong’s revival of Fences is impressively honed, with the simmering first act infusing significance into the explosive second.
